mappings.note: Which fuel leaves ash compares fuels on a property of burning. Not LO-32, because no fuel is sorted into a class.
The zone a goldsmith uses is part of the structure of a flame, named verbatim in LO-35. Not LO-42, because the item asks which zone rather than how to use a blowpipe.
Deciding whether rusting counts as combustion places a process in or out of a class. Not LO-35, because no mechanism is explained.
Deciding whether the Sun's output is combustion is the same in-or-out classification. Kept apart from the item asking what the solar process actually is, which explains it.
Naming nuclear fusion as the source of the Sun's heat explains a process. Not LO-32, because the item states the mechanism rather than judging a class.
Defining ignition temperature explains a key idea of the combustion process. Not LO-33, which needs an investigation to be conducted rather than a definition recalled.
Which substance a matchstick can light identifies the inflammable class. Not LO-34, because no cause is traced.
A matchstick not igniting on its own because its ignition temperature is high relates an observation to its cause. Not LO-35, which is used for the definition of that temperature.
The gas that puts out fire is fire-safety science applied in daily life. Not LO-40, which would require a working extinguisher to be built.
Naming very fast burning rapid combustion sorts combustion into its types. Not LO-35, because a class is named rather than a process explained.
The coldest zone of a candle is part of the structure of a flame. Grouped with the other flame-zone items.
What smoke contains describes what combustion gives off. Not LO-34, because no effect is traced to a cause.
The colour of the non-luminous zone describes the flame's structure. Grouped with the other flame-zone items.
The fuel with the highest calorific value compares fuels on a property. Not LO-43, because no environmental choice is made.
The fuel replacing petrol and diesel is chosen to cut pollution, an environmental judgement. Not LO-31, which covers comparing fuels on their burning properties.
Which substance burns without a flame differentiates fuels by how they burn. Not LO-35, because no part of a flame is described.
The best automobile fuel turns on the ideal-fuel criteria, pollution among them. Grouped with the other clean-fuel choices.
Which gas causes global warming relates a phenomenon to its cause. Not LO-43, because no protective action is proposed.

The unit of calorific value is a measurement question, and the frame's only measurement outcome, LO-37, covers angles of incidence and reflection only. Cited at competency level because no learning outcome reaches it.
The hottest zone of a candle flame is the structure of a flame. Grouped with the other flame-zone items.
Defining combustion as reaction with oxygen giving heat explains the process. Not LO-36, because no equation is written.
Which substance burns with a flame differentiates materials by burning behaviour. Not LO-32, because no class is named.
Magnesium burning in air to give magnesium oxide is a metal-air reaction, LO-36 word for word. Not LO-35, because a reaction product rather than a process is asked.
Picking the non-combustible substance is the combustible/non-combustible classification. Not LO-31, because membership rather than a property comparison is tested.
The conditions under which combustion takes place is the query LO-33 names verbatim. Not LO-35, because the item lists requirements rather than explaining the flame.
The smoke-free fuel is an environmental choice between fuels. Not LO-31, which covers burning properties without the pollution judgement.
Coal being mainly carbon is material composition. Not LO-32, because no class is assigned.
Carbon monoxide arising from incomplete combustion relates a hazard to its cause. Not LO-36, because it is the consequence of poor burning rather than a written equation.
The natural solid fuel sorts fuels by origin and state. Not LO-31, because a class member rather than a property is asked for.
The fuel that burns without polluting is an environmental choice. Grouped with the other clean-fuel items.
Which substance gives heat and light on burning identifies the fuel class. Not LO-35, because no process is explained.
The Sun's process named as fusion explains where its heat and light come from. Not LO-32, because the item states the mechanism rather than judging a class.
Coal burning with a glow rather than a flame differentiates fuels by burning behaviour. Not LO-35, because no flame structure is described.
Charcoal burnt in a closed room producing carbon monoxide relates a danger to its cause. Grouped with the incomplete-combustion item.
Substances with low ignition temperature catching fire easily relates a property to its consequence. Not LO-35, which is used for the definition of ignition temperature.
CNG and LPG as examples of gaseous fuels is classification of fuels. Not LO-31, because a class rather than a property is assigned.
Defining ignition temperature explains a key idea of combustion. Duplicate in substance of the earlier definition item.
Combustion described as a chemical process explains what it is. Not LO-32, because no type of combustion is named.
The products of combustion, carbon dioxide and water, are the reaction outputs LO-36 covers. Not LO-35, because products rather than the flame are asked for.
The number of zones in a flame is the structure of a flame, named verbatim in LO-35. Grouped with the other flame-zone items.
